transcript:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate on internal SRV lookups in us-east-1 (resolver egress path split). Symptoms: ~30% SRV resolution failures for platform services, elevated 5xx from internal API chains. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/resolver-egress
elaine: Paging. I'm oncall. seeing spike in 5xx across platform-prod, correlation with SRV lookup timeouts to consul in us-east-1b
ashwin: I see asymmetric egress routes from our resolver fleet in us-east-1a -> some flows going via peering path hitting a noisy NAT GW. packet drops reported at 10.3.45.0/24
jacob: Any recent network changes? We pushed a peering policy update ~30m ago for cost optimization
elaine: yes that matches timeline. can we roll back that peering policy or pin resolver egress to the primary path?
maria: Customer impact: a few enterprise customers reported increased latency and occasional failures in the chat ingestion pipeline. Support has queued incidents but no escalations yet.
ashwin: Rolling back peering policy now. command: `gcloud compute network-peering update --name=us-east1-peer --remove-route-configuration` (dryrun -> apply)
elaine: meanwhile can we point the resolver pod affinity to regional egress? quick mitigation: force resolver pods to use local nat gw via nodeSelector + taint? that's heavy
kevin: Runtime note: our service discovery library retries SRV lookup 3x with 200ms backoff and treats NX as terminal -> that exacerbates 5xx. We can deploy a hotfix to treat transient errors as retryable for 5s window
jacob: rollback applied. monitoring shows drop in packet error rates on 10.3.45.0/24 after ~45s
incident-bot: Deploy bot: Started rollout of platform-runtime patch `sd-retry-fix v2.4.1` to canary (3 pods) — https://redwood.internal/deploys/12345
elaine: running quick dig tests from resolver pod:
```
# dig +short SRV _api._tcp.service.svc.cluster.local @127.0.0.53
; timeout after 2 seconds
```
ashwin: tcpdump on egress shows RSTs when going through the alternate path. snippet:
```
15:12:03.123456 IP 10.1.4.12.54321 > 10.3.45.9.53: UDP, length 78
15:12:03.123789 IP 10.3.45.9 > 10.1.4.12: ICMP  Destination unreachable (Fragmentation needed)
```
kevin: can we add a fallback that uses cached SRV responses from the Consul agent cache for 1s while we stabilize
jacob: added HTTP 503 fallback with client-side backoff policy for the chat ingestion route to reduce user-visible errors
maria: update for customers: posting to status page that we're investigating elevated internal service failures in us-east (no data exfiltration, limited service degradation). Draft: "We are experiencing internal service discovery failures impacting request routing for some customers in US East. Engineers are investigating; retrying requests will likely succeed within a few seconds."
elaine: deploy bot reports canary healthy after runtime patch. Starting rollout to 40%.
incident-bot: Alert: SRV failure rate decreased to 9% (was 32%). Latency on platform-prod down ~15% from peak
ashwin: still seeing some sporadic drops on cross-AZ peering path. I recommend marking that path as deprioritized in smart-routing until packet loss < 0.5%
jacob: done: smart-routing config updated to prefer direct egress for resolver service in us-east. change id cfg-9876
elaine: handoff: I'm running the mitigation and will stay on for 30 more minutes, then hand off to @oncall-next. Next oncall please verify that: 1) SRV error rate < 2% 2) no new customer escalations 3) patch rollout complete
oncall-next: ack, I'll take on the follow-up. I'll validation-check in 30m and run synthetic SRV lookups across AZs
maria: support will hold customer updates until after next check. no major escalations yet, keeping watch
kevin: postmortem note: root cause appears to be peering route config change combined with aggressive runtime NX handling -> plan: add circuit-breaker and consul-agent local cache TTL bump, and preflight peering changes in canary, update runbook
elaine: thanks all. closing pager for now, moving to monitoring phase. please add any follow-up action items to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2164321000
incident-bot: INCIDENT: status moved to monitoring. pages suppressed.
